sara-a-princess-the-story-of-a-noble-gir: Fannie Newberry's story for girls follows Sara, a young heroine whose noble spirit earns her the story's royal nickname. Through small trials at home and among friends, she learns kindness, courage, and what it means to act like a true princess of character. Written in the warm moral style of its era, the book aims to both entertain and shape its young readers.
light-o-the-morning-the-story-of-an-iris: L. T. Meade tells of an Irish girl, a light o' the morning, whose bright spirit conquers hardship. Her tale of Ireland charmed young readers everywhere. Warm, wholesome, and full of Irish charm. Her laughter brightens every chapter of this sunny Irish tale.
the-daughter-of-the-chieftain-the-story-: Edward Ellis tells of the daughter of the chieftain — an Indian girl's story of the frontier — with his usual thrilling pace. Dangers, escapes, and woodland lore abound on every page. Classic Ellis adventure for boys. Forest trails and tribal councils fill this stirring frontier tale.
